column2: 英语原作 tricker，借自荷兰语 trekker（拉手、拉绳）← trekken（拉、拖）
column3: the lever you pull to fire a gun, or the thing that sets something off
column5: He kept his finger off the trigger.|Dust can trigger an attack of asthma.
column6: the small pull that releases a much bigger action – 轻轻一拉，放出一个大得多的动作
column7: 扳机：枪上供手指扣动的那个小杆|触发：一件小事引出后面一连串反应

column2: 中古英语 trimen ← 古英语 trymman（使坚固）← 原始日耳曼语 *trumjaną（加固）← *trumaz（结实的）
column3: to cut small amounts off to make something neat
column5: He trimmed the hedge on Sunday.|They trimmed the budget by a tenth.
column6: cutting off just the excess so the shape comes out even – 只剪掉多出来那点，让形状齐整
column7: 修剪：剪去多余的枝叶或头发|削减：把预算或人数减掉一部分|齐整的：经过这样处理后的那种样子

column2: 中古英语 trippen（轻快踏步、跳跃），或 ← 古法语 triper（跳跃、踢），或 ← 中古荷兰语 trippen（轻踏、绊）；与 trap、tramp 同支
column3: a short journey, or to catch the foot and stumble
column5: They took a trip to the coast.|She tripped over the doorstep.
column6: a light quick movement of the feet, and the short journey it makes – 脚步轻快的一下，以及由此走成的短程
column7: 短途出行：不远的一趟往来|绊倒：脚被挂住而失去平衡|失足：踏错一步这个动作

column2: 中古英语借自古法语 triomphe ← 拉丁语 triumphus（凯旋游行）← 希腊语 thriambos
column3: a great victory, or the joy that comes with it
column5: The win was a personal triumph.|They returned home in triumph.
column6: a victory large enough to be paraded – 大到值得游街庆祝的那种胜利
column7: 胜利：赢下来这件事|凯旋：得胜归来时那种荣耀场面

column2: 英语 trolley 1823 年始见，本义「小车」，出自方言（萨福克），或由 troll（滚动）＋ 指小后缀 -ey 构成
column3: a small vehicle on wheels for carrying things
column5: She pushed a trolley round the aisles.|The tea trolley came at eleven.
column6: a small wheeled frame pushed along to carry things – 推着走的带轮小架，用来载物
column7: 手推车：超市或车站里推着装货的那种|餐车：推着送茶点的那种小车

column2: 英语 troop 1545 年始见，借自法语 troupe ← 中古法语 trope ← 古法语 trupe，更早词源不明；与德语 Dorf（村）或同源
column3: a group of soldiers, or any organized group
column5: Troops moved in at dawn.|A troop of scouts camped nearby.
column6: a body of people moving and acting as one – 成群一起行动的一批人
column7: 部队：成建制的士兵|一队人：泛指结伴同行的一群

column2: 源自晚期拉丁语 tropicus（与至点有关的）← 希腊语 tropikos（转折的）← trope（转、至点）
column3: either of the two lines of latitude marking where the sun turns back
column5: The ship crossed the tropic of Cancer.|Rainfall is heavy in the tropics.
column6: the latitude where the overhead sun turns back – 太阳直射到此便折回的那条纬线
column7: 回归线：南北各一条的那两条纬线|热带：这两条线之间的地带

column2: 由 tropic ＋ -al 构成；tropic 一支 ← 希腊语 tropikos（转折的）← trope（转）
column3: belonging to the hot wet region near the equator
column5: Tropical storms hit the coast each year.|The plant needs a tropical climate.
column6: of the hot damp belt where the sun stands overhead – 属于日光直射、又热又湿那一带的
column7: 热带的：位于或来自那一地带|湿热的：形容那种又潮又热的气候

column2: 中古英语 troublen ← 古法语 troubler ← 通俗拉丁语 *turbulare ← 拉丁语 turbula（小骚乱），是 turba（骚动、人群）的指小形
column3: difficulty or a problem, or to cause worry
column5: The engine gave us trouble all week.|Sorry to trouble you so late.
column6: something that stirs up what was running smoothly – 把本来顺当的事搅乱的那件东西
column7: 麻烦：难办、费事的情况|毛病：机器或身体出的那个问题|费心：劳烦对方为自己出力

column2: 由 trouble ＋ 形容词后缀 -some 构成；trouble 一支 ← 古法语 troubler ← 拉丁语 turba（骚动）
column3: causing difficulty over and over
column5: The leak proved troublesome all winter.|He asked a troublesome question.
column6: keeping on causing difficulty rather than settling – 一直添乱，不肯了结
column7: 麻烦的：反复出问题、费事|难对付的：不易处置，让人头疼

column2: 英语 trousers 1610 年代始见，由早期 trouse 加成对之物的复数词尾而来 ← 中古爱尔兰语 triubus（紧身短裤）← 古爱尔兰语 tribus，更早词源不明
column3: a piece of clothing covering the legs separately
column5: He wore grey trousers and a white shirt.|These trousers need taking up.
column6: a garment that sheathes each leg on its own – 两条腿各套一筒的那件衣服
column7: 长裤：盖到脚踝的那种|裤子：这类衣物的通称

column2: 英语 truck 或截自 truckle（小轮）← 拉丁语 trochus（铁环、轮）← 希腊语 trochos（轮）
column3: a large road vehicle for carrying goods
column5: A truck blocked the narrow lane.|They loaded the truck by hand.
column6: a large vehicle built to haul loads by road – 专为在路上载重而造的大车
column7: 卡车：运货的那种大车|载重车：强调它承重这一用途

column2: 中古英语 trewe ← 古英语 trēowe（忠实的、真实的）← 原始日耳曼语 *triwwiz ← 原始印欧语 *drew-（坚实、硬）；与 tree 同支，本义「像树一样牢靠」
column3: agreeing with the facts, or loyal
column5: Is it true that she resigned?|He stayed true to his word.
column6: standing firm against the facts, as a tree stands – 拿事实来量也立得住，像树那样牢
column7: 真实的：与事实相符|确实的：经核对无误|忠实的：对人对诺言立得住，不变节

column2: 中古英语 trumpet ← 古法语 trompette，是 trompe（号角）的指小形 ← 法兰克语 *trumpa（号），拟声；取代了古英语 bīeme
column3: a brass instrument played by blowing, with a bright loud sound
column5: He plays trumpet in a jazz band.|A trumpet sounded from the tower.
column6: a brass tube blown to give a bright carrying note – 铜管吹出的那种明亮而传得远的音
column7: 小号：乐队里那件铜管乐器|喇叭：形状与用途相类的那种发声器

column2: 中古英语 tronke ← 古法语 tronc（树干、钱柜）← 拉丁语 truncus（砍去枝梢的树干）；与 truncate 同源
column3: the thick main stem of a tree, or a large box for travelling
column5: Ivy covered the whole trunk.|She packed her clothes in an old trunk.
column6: the thick main body left when the branches are cut away – 砍掉枝梢后剩下的那根粗主体
column7: 树干：树的主体那根粗柱|大箱子：形似一段树干的那种旅行箱|象鼻：象脸前那根粗长的，形状也像一段干

column2: 中古英语 trust（信托、庇护），或出自未见记载的古英语 *trust ← 原始日耳曼语 *traustą 的零级变体 ← 原始印欧语 *deru-（坚实、硬）；与 true、tree 同支
column3: a firm belief that someone will not let you down
column5: She placed her trust in him.|The money is held in trust for the children.
column6: resting your weight on someone as on firm ground – 把重量放到对方身上，像踩在实地上
column7: 信任：相信对方不会失约|信赖：更深一层，凡事都靠得住|托管：把财产交人代管，正是靠这份相信

column2: 中古英语 trouthe，即 true ＋ 抽象名词后缀 -th；true 一支 ← 古英语 trēowe（忠实的、真实的）← 原始印欧语 *drew-（坚实）
column3: what is in accordance with fact
column5: He finally told the truth.|There is some truth in that claim.
column6: the way things actually stand, once checked – 核过之后事情实际是怎样
column7: 真相：某件事实际的情形|实情：不加掩饰的那份情况|真理：普遍成立、经得住检验的道理

column2: 中古英语 trien（筛选、甄别、审案）← 盎格鲁诺曼语 trier ← 古法语 trier（挑选、分开），更早词源不明
column3: to make an attempt at something
column5: She tried to open the jar with a cloth.|Try the other key before you give up.
column6: putting effort in to see whether it works – 使一份力，看行不行得通
column7: 试：动手做一下看结果|尝试：着手试着做某事|努力：把这份使力延长、加重

column2: 中古英语 tubbe ← 中古荷兰语 tubbe 或中古低地德语 tobbe，更早词源不明；与 tube 无关
column3: a wide open container for water or for holding things
column5: She filled the tub with warm water.|Buy a tub of ice cream.
column6: a wide open vessel deeper than it is tall – 口宽、壁直的敞口容器
column7: 盆：口大而浅的那种|桶：壁直而深的那种|浴缸：供人洗浴的那个大容器

column2: 源自中古法语 tube ← 拉丁语 tubus（管），与 tuba（长号）相关，更早词源不明
column3: a long hollow cylinder for liquid or gas to pass through
column5: Water ran through a rubber tube.|He takes the tube to work.
column6: a long hollow cylinder for something to pass along inside – 中空的长筒，东西在里面通过
column7: 管：中空的细长筒|管子：日常说法，义同|地铁：伦敦地铁因隧道呈圆筒状而得此俗名

column2: 中古英语 tuken（拉扯、抻布）← 古英语 tūcian（折磨）与中古荷兰语 tucken（塞）← 原始日耳曼语 *teug-（拉）← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（拉）；与 touch 同源
column3: to push a loose edge into a narrow space so it stays
column5: He tucked his shirt into his trousers.|She tucked the child into bed.
column6: pushing a loose edge in so it is held fast – 把松着的边推进去，让它别住
column7: 折进：把边缘折起塞入|收进：把露出的部分收到里面|掩好：把被子边压到身下，使人裹紧

column2: 中古英语 tuggen ← 古英语 togian（拖）← 原始日耳曼语 *tugōną（拉、拽）← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（拉）；与 tow 同源
column3: to pull hard with a short movement
column5: He tugged at the rope with both hands.|A tug guided the ship into port.
column6: one short hard pull rather than a steady draw – 短促用力拉一下，不是匀速拖
column7: 用力拉：使劲拉一把|猛拽：更猛更短的那一下|拖船：专门拉别的船的那种小船

column2: 中古英语 ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 tuycioun ← 古法语 tuicion ← 拉丁语 tuitio（看守、保护）← tueri（看守、照看）；与 tutor 同支
column3: teaching given to one student or a small group, or the fee for it
column5: She gives private tuition in maths.|Tuition has risen again this year.
column6: close teaching under someone's watch – 在人看着的情况下逐点教
column7: 辅导：一对一或小组的那种教|教学：泛指教授这件事|学费：为受教所付的那笔钱

column2: 中古英语 tumblen（一再翻倒），是 tumben（跌、跳）的反复体 ← 古英语 tumbian ← 原始日耳曼语 *tūmōną（转动）
column3: to fall while turning over
column5: The boxes tumbled off the shelf.|Share prices tumbled overnight on the news.
column6: falling while rolling over rather than straight down – 边翻边落，不是直直坠下
column7: 跌落：从高处掉下来|翻滚：落时不断翻转|暴跌：把这种翻着落用到价格上

column2: 中古英语 tumour ← 古法语 tumour ← 拉丁语 tumor（肿）← tumeō（鼓起、肿胀）← 原始印欧语 *tewh₂-（隆起）；与 thumb 同支
column3: a swollen mass of abnormal cells in the body
column5: The scan showed a small tumour.|The tumour turned out to be harmless.
column6: a lump of cells that keeps growing where it should not – 一团细胞在不该长的地方一直长
column7: 肿瘤：医学上的正式称法|瘤：口语与复合词里的简称

column2: 中古英语 tune，是 tone 的变体 ← 古法语 ton ← 拉丁语 tonus ← 希腊语 tonos（音）
column3: a series of musical notes that make a recognizable whole, or to adjust pitch
column5: She hummed a familiar tune.|He tuned the guitar before playing.
column6: notes in an order one can recognize, and the setting right of pitch – 排得能让人认出的一串音，以及把音高校准
column7: 曲调：能哼出来、认得出的那一串音|调音：把乐器音高校到准|调准：把设备调到该有的状态

column2: 源自中古法语 tonnelle（网）或 tonel（小桶），是古法语 tonne（桶）的指小形，更早词源不明；与 tun（大桶）相关
column3: a passage dug underground or through a hill
column5: The train entered a long tunnel.|Prisoners dug a tunnel under the wall.
column6: a passage bored through so that one can go beyond – 打穿出来的通路，为的是过到那一边
column7: 隧道：穿山或穿水的那种大通路|地道：地下挖出的那种窄通路

column2: 截自 turkeycock；原指从土耳其贩入欧洲的珍珠鸡，后转指北美这种外形相近的大鸟
column3: a large bird raised for meat
column5: They roast a turkey every Christmas.|The turkeys are kept in the far pen.
column6: a large farm bird with a fanning tail, eaten at feasts – 尾羽能展开的大型家禽，节庆时食用

column2: 由动词短语 turn over 转成的名词；turn 一支 ← 古英语 turnian ← 拉丁语 tornare（车削、旋转）
column3: the total amount of business done, or the rate at which people leave and are replaced
column5: The shop has a turnover of two million.|Staff turnover is high in that department.
column6: how much passes through and is replaced over a period – 一段时间里过手并被换掉的量
column7: 营业额：一段时间做成的生意总额|人员流动率：员工离去与补进的快慢

column2: 中古英语 tutour ← 古法语 tuteur ← 拉丁语 tutor（看守者、保护人）← tueor（保护）；与 tuition 同支
column3: a teacher who works with one student or a small group
column5: His tutor set extra reading each week.|They hired a tutor for the twins.
column6: a teacher who watches over one learner closely – 盯着一个学生逐点教的那种老师
column7: 导师：学院里指导某几名学生的教师|家庭教师：上门单独授课的那种
